analytic.title: Reliable Routing of Time-Triggered Traffic in Time Sensitive Networks

div.p: With the continuous evolution of industrial network technology, industrial production has higher and higher requirements for reliability and real-time performance. At present, Time Sensitive Networks (TSN) has become one of the evolution directions of the next generation network bearing technology. In TSN, redundancy is usually adopted to meet the reliability requirements of Time-Triggered (TT) flow. However, a large amount of bandwidth consumption caused by redundancy is also inevitable, which will directly affect the schedulability of TT flows. Therefore, this paper proposes a Genetically based Reliable Routing algorithm (GRR) based on Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER) standard, which provides reliable and non-overlapping routes for different copies of each TT flow. It not only guarantees the reliability of the TT flow, but also increases its schedulability, so as to meet the needs of industrial applications. Through simulation experiments, compared with the existing methods, the reliability of the proposed reliable routing algorithm is improved by 2.08% on average and the schedulability is improved by 6.3% on average.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: At present, the fourth Industrial Revolution is sweeping the world in an unprecedented manner. In fact, Germany put forward this concept at the Hannover MESse in 2013, and described the vision of the future manufacturing industry. The core of this revolution lies in the high integration of networking, information technology and intelligence. In this revolution, the industrial Internet exists as a key enabling technology. Industrial Internet is the product of the deep integration of the new generation of information technology and the manufacturing industry. In essence, it is to build a new manufacturing and service system by comprehensively connecting people, machines, materials and systems in the production chain [1].

In the architecture of industrial Internet, network system is the foundation, while the existing industrial Ethernet technologies, such as PROFINET, Ethernet CAT, TTEthernet, etc., have the problems of poor interoperability and high cost [2] [3]. Time Sensitive Networks(TSN) emerged as a solution. It is a general standard based on Ethernet technology, which not only guarantees the deterministic delay and bandwidth, but also reduces the cost and realizes the integration of industrial control network and industrial information network. To this end, the 802.1 Working Group developed a set of standards, but the TSN standard does not involve the study of routing and scheduling algorithms, so additional consideration is needed.

In recent work, some scholars proposed to combine routing and scheduling planning. All literatures [4] and [5] plan routing and scheduling jointly based on ILP formula, which provides lower communication delay and improves traffic schedulability. Li et al. proposed a new algorithm for joint routing and scheduling planning to eliminate the uncertain queuing delay (or interruption) caused by unexpected transmission conflicts of Time-Triggered (TT) flows, and built a scheduling model that enables TT and non-TT flows to coexist while meeting the endto-end delay requirements of all TT flows [6]. The above literature does not consider the reliability requirements of the network. In addition, although this joint planning method improves the schedulability of traffic, it is more suitable for the small-scale network due to the large solution space, but it is unable to cope with the large scale and heavy load network. In literature [7], the purpose of network fault tolerance is achieved by copying the whole network. Literature [8] realizes network fault tolerance by determining a fault-tolerant network topology. However, the cost of energy consumption and time is huge no matter how to copy the network or build the fault-tolerant network topology.

In TSN, redundancy is usually adopted to meet the reliability requirements of TT flows. However, a large amount of bandwidth consumption caused by redundancy is inevitable, which will directly affect the schedulability of TT flows. Therefore, this paper proposes a Genetically based Reliable Routing algorithm (GRR) based on Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER) standard, which provides reliable and non-overlapping routes for different copies of each TT flow. It not only guarantees the reliability of the TT flow, but also increases its schedulability, so as to meet the needs of industrial applications.

The contributions of this paper are summarized as follows, using the mathematical method of Poisson distribution, the reliability analysis model is constructed, and the average probability of successful transmission of each flow is used to measure the reliability of the network; in order to obtain a highly reliable route, this paper selects the routes in the pre-processing part of the algorithm, and then uses simulated annealing genetic algorithm to provide reliable and non-overlapping routes for different copies of each TT flow; in simulated annealing genetic algorithm, a fitness function which can measure the degree of network conflict is proposed by combining the parameters of flow; a test case is developed based on the actual industrial application to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

div.head: A. System Model
div.p: An actual TSN network consists of a terminal system, TSN switches, and Ethernet-based full duplex physical links. The source and destination of all flows can only be the terminal system. It is assumed that all TSN switches and terminal systems on the network comply with the 802.1as standard and realize clock synchronization. Of course, all TSN switches and terminal systems need to support the 802.1Qbv standard. In addition, the whole time-sensitive network adopts the fully set Chinese-style configuration model. All the routing and scheduling algorithms are completed on the control layer. The controller performs offline calculation and generates a static scheduling table, which is then sent to the TSN switch. The network topology is modeled as a directed graph , where represents the set of all communication nodes in the network, consisting of a terminal system and a TSN switch . indicates the set of all links. The link between and of any two devices corresponds to two unidirectional links and .

div.head: B. Application Model
div.p: This article considers a set of time-sensitive applications with reliability requirements that can be represented by timetriggered flows. In the 802.1CB standard, a flow is defined as a one-way flow of time-sensitive data from one source to one or more destinations. Each flow can be represented by tuples , where and represent the source and target nodes of the flow, respectively. The cycle size of the flow and the data size sent per cycle are represented by and respectively. represents the maximum end-toend delay required by the flow, i.e. the cutoff time. If the actual end-to-end delay of a flow meets the maximum end-to-end delay requirement of the flow, the flow is said to be schedulable. represents the redundancy level of the flow, i.e. the number of copies sent by the flow. According to the 802.1CB standard, the layout of FRER functional components is very flexible. In this paper, we consider the following scenario. Only edge switches in the network have frame copy and erase capabilities, that is, frames will only be copied on the first TSN switch on the selected path and eliminated on the last TSN switch.

div.head: C. Reliability Analysis Model
div.p: Because the main work of this paper is to improve the schedulability of TT flow as far as possible on the premise of ensuring certain reliability. Therefore, if you blindly add more copies of the flow, the reliability of the flow will be improved, but the network will become crowded, and the schedulability of the TT flow will be decreased. In this case, you need to perform reliability evaluation in advance, set a certain redundancy level for the flow, and select a link with higher reliability. Here, the reliability probability , which is obtained from the average value of the successful transmission probability of each flow in the network, is used to measure the reliability of the network. In order to facilitate the study, the redundancy level of all flows is set to 2.

div.head: III. RELIABLE ROUTING ALGORITHM BASED ON GENETIC
div.p: The algorithm can be divided into two steps. Firstly, the preprocessing is carried out to remove the routes whose reliability is lower than the reliability threshold, so as to provide the candidate route set for the following algorithm. Then simulated annealing genetic algorithm is used to get the final result.

div.head: A. Preprocessing
div.p: In order to obtain routes with higher reliability and reduce the search space of the routing algorithm, the pre-processing part is divided into the following three steps. First, all possible routes are generated for each TT flow, and the probability of successful transmission of each TT flow on the corresponding route is calculated by using the reliability analysis model. The advantage of this is that possible excellent solutions will not be lost.

Then, in order to generate more reliable routes for each TT flow within the limited redundancy level, a reliability probability threshold should be set here to remove the routes whose reliability is lower than the reliability probability threshold from all possible routes. Finally, in order to prevent the TT flow from being transmitted due to the failure of the routes selected by different copies of the TT flow on the overlapping link, non-overlapping routes are selected for different copies of the TT flow in this algorithm. To this end, the following definition is given. A nonoverlapping route group of can be represented by the following formula, (7) It represents a set of routes from the source node to the target node, and there is no link overlap between these routes, and the number of a set of routes is equal to the redundancy level of . div.head: B. Simulated Annealing Genetic Algorithms
div.p: Selecting non-overlapping routing groups from the nonoverlapping routing set of each flow to get the final routing scheme can be considered as a combinatorial optimization problem. In this paper, genetic algorithm is adopted to solve the combinatorial optimization problem, and the simulated annealing algorithm is introduced to improve the selection operator of the genetic algorithm, which effectively avoids the precocious convergence of the algorithm. div.head: 3) Selection operator
div.p: The selection operator is the survival of well-adapted individuals and the elimination of ill-adapted individuals, and in doing so the good genes are preserved. The commonly used algorithms in the selection operator include roulette, tournament algorithm, etc., but this will make the whole algorithm appear precocious phenomenon, so as to converge to the local optimal solution. div.head: 4) Crossover and mutation operators
div.p: Crossover operator allows genes to exchange, thus producing better individuals. In this algorithm, single point crossover is adopted, allowing non-overlapping routing groups of different individuals in the same position to exchange, so as to ensure that after crossing, the routes corresponding to different copies of each flow are still non-overlapping routes. As shown in Figure 1, it is assumed that there are three flows in the network, and each gene is randomly selected from the nonoverlapping routing set corresponding to the flow.

Mutation operator can make the population acquire new genes, and avoid the algorithm convergence too early. In this algorithm, a new non-overlapping routing group is randomly selected from the corresponding non-overlapping routing set to replace the original non-overlapping routing group.

div.head: IV. SIMULATION EXPERIMENT AND RESULT ANALYSIS
div.p: In order to verify the effectiveness of GRR method, this paper conducts a series of experiments based on python framework on an Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8250U processor with 1.60GHz and 8GB RAM. In order to illustrate the advantages of GRR method in traffic schedulability, The scheduling experiment is completed on Gurobi solver using integer linear programming method. In the experiment, networkX, a network As can be seen from the figure, when the number of added TT flows keeps increasing, the network becomes crowded. No matter which algorithm is used, the number of dispatchable flows tends to decline. When the route generated by SR algorithm is used for traffic scheduling, the number of schedulable flows is greater than that of the other two algorithms. This is because the SR algorithm has no redundant paths. When the redundancy level is 2, the traffic required by the SR algorithm is equal to half of that of other algorithms, so the number of schedulable flows will naturally be greater than that of other algorithms. The SMR algorithm only takes the two shortest routes as redundant routes and does not optimize the selected routes. As a result, routes used by a large number of flows are bound to overlap, and the number of dispatchable flows decreases. GRR algorithm uses heuristic algorithm to optimize routes. Compared with SMR algorithm which also adopts spatial redundancy, the number of schedulable flows is improved. Moreover, the more complex the network is, the larger the space for route optimization selection is for GRR algorithm, so the better the effect is. Overall, the schedulability of GRR algorithm is improved by 6.3% compared with SMR algorithm.

To sum up, SR algorithm sacrifices reliability in exchange for high schedulability, while SMR algorithm sacrifices schedulability in exchange for high reliability. The GRR algorithm proposed in this paper can increase its schedulability on the premise of ensuring certain reliability.

V. CONCLUOSION In this paper, a reliable routing algorithm based on heredity is proposed to provide reliable and non-overlapping routes for different copies of each TT flow. In order to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, ILP method is used for scheduling. Through the simulation experiment, compared with the traditional routing method, the proposed algorithm can ensure the reliability of the TT flow and increase its schedulability. In future work, we will extend the scheduling method to further improve TT flow schedulability.

The current research on reliable routing algorithm does not provide the source code, so it is impossible to compare its performance. Therefore, this paper uses the existing Shortest Routing algorithm (SR) and Shortest Multipath Routing algorithm (SMR) as the benchmark to test the effectiveness of this algorithm. Due to limited space, this article does not elaborate on it. The following part will illustrate the effectiveness of this algorithm from the perspectives of reliability and schedulability.

div.head: A. Analysis of Reliability
div.p: In the reliability analysis experiment, 20 test cases were randomly constructed, and 30 flows were added to each case. The results were averaged. GRR, SR and SMR algorithms were used to conduct experiments on two topologies with the number of TSN switches being 7 and 10, denoted as topology 1 and topology 2 respectively. In each topology, the number of links prone to failure n varied from 1 to 4. The reliability probability of each case was calculated using the formula proposed in the reliability analysis model. The reliability probability threshold is set as 0.95 in the GRR algorithm, and the following figure is obtained, where the x-coordinate represents the number of links prone to failure n, and the y-coordinate represents the reliability probability .

The reliability analysis of topology 1 is carried out in Figure 2. When n changes from 1 to 4, the network reliability probability of GRR algorithm decreases by 0.5%, SR algorithm by 8.93%, and SMR algorithm by 5.03%. The reliability analysis of topology 2 is carried out in Figure 3. when n changes from 1 to 4, GRR algorithm decreases by 0.69%, SR algorithm decreases by 7.52%, and SMR algorithm decreases by 4.74%.

Specific analysis shows that the reliability probability of the network using SR algorithm is lower than that of the other two algorithms due to the lack of reliability consideration. When increases, the route obtained by using SR algorithm is more likely to contain faulty links. Therefore, the reliability probability of the network using this algorithm shows a declining trend. In addition, compared with the experiments on topology 1 and Topology 2, when the network becomes complicated, the number of links contained in the shortest route obtained by the SR algorithm may also become more, so the possibility of containing faulty links also becomes higher, so its reliability probability decreases. In the same topology, the reliability probability tends to decline with the increase of . In different topologies, the more complex the topology is, the lower the reliability probability is. However, since the SMR algorithm adopts multi-path redundant routing, the overall reliability probability is much higher than that of the SR algorithm. Compared with SMR algorithm, the network reliability probability of GRR algorithm is 2.08% higher on the whole, and the network reliability probability of GRR algorithm is relatively stable due to the screening of reliable routes in the algorithm.

div.head: B. Analysis of Schedulability
div.p: In the schedulability analysis experiment, 50 test cases were randomly constructed, and the three algorithms GRR, SR and SMR were used to conduct the experiment on Topology 1 and Topology 2 respectively. The number of TT flows added to each topology was 20, 30 and 40, respectively. The percentage of the number of schedulable flows in all test cases is used as the representation of schedulability.
